topPRs.title: feat: U19 permissionless flip for karst-u19-alpha + beta-0 correction (CANNON_KONA)
topPRs.author: Wazabie
topPRs.body:
Split out of #1440. Contains the **karst-u19-alpha** permissionless rollout, the **karst-u19-beta-0** permissioned correction, and the `SetDisputeGameImpl` template extension they need. The ink/uni standard-chain U19 tasks and the OPCMUpgradeV700 / SuperchainAddressRegistry fixes stay in #1440.

## Tasks (Sepolia, shared PAO Safe `0x8E851F7d8bAeaD95F592847a020cAC7A062dafd9`)

| # | Chain | Action | Template |
|---|---|---|---|
| 092 | karst-u19-alpha-1 | wire CANNON_KONA (8) reusing `0x2DDA` + alpha kona prestate `0x03ff5c52…`; permissioned (1) prestate → `0xdead`; game 0 stays `0x0` | SetDisputeGameImpl |
| 093 | karst-u19-alpha-1 | `respectedGameType` → 8 | SetRespectedGameTypeTemplate |
| 094 | karst-u19-alpha-0 | permissioned (1) prestate → `0xdead` (stays permissioned; no game 8) | SetDisputeGameImpl |
| 095 | karst-u19-beta-0 | `respectedGameType` 8 → 1 (correction) | SetRespectedGameTypeTemplate |
| 096 | karst-u19-beta-0 | zero CANNON_KONA (8) impl (correction) | SetDisputeGameImpl |

Resulting end-states match the U19 clarification (permissioned: respected 1 + no game 8; permissionless: respected 8 + kona, with game 1 fallback at `0xdead`):
- **alpha-1** permissionless: g0=`0x0`, g1=`0xe1dF`/`0xdead`, g8=`0x2DDA`/kona, respected **8**
- **alpha-0** permissioned: g0=`0x0`, g1=`0xe1dF`/`0xdead`, g8=`0x0`, respected **1**
- **beta-0** permissioned (corrected from an earlier respected=8 / kona-wired state): g8=`0x0`, respected **1**

## Template change
`SetDisputeGameImpl` gains an optional `[[konaGameImplConfig]]` block (game type 8) — backward-compatible; existing FDG/PDG tasks unaffected. Supports wire (impl + 124-byte gameArgs) and disable (impl `0x0`).

## Prestate
Alpha kona prestate `0x03ff5c52c5a21d238e01c53158f4dcc26de9a35d138b010c14874699c7973b8d` built reproducibly from `kona-client/v1.6.0-rc.1` (monorepo @ `1e4fe99…`) embedding both alpha chains; embedded-config check passed; uploaded to `gs://oplabs-network-data/proofs/kona/cannon/`.

## Verification & caveats
- Full 092→096 stack simulates clean on `main`.
- Hashes in each VALIDATION.md were captured at assumed sequential nonces 8–12. The Safe is shared across alpha-0/alpha-1/beta-0/beta-1; **re-verify nonce/hash at signing**. beta-0 (095/096) is intended as a **separate signing batch** — re-pin if executed ahead of the alpha rollout.
- No regression test yet for the new `konaGameImplConfig` path (existing `Regression.t.sol` SetDisputeGameImpl coverage still passes).

topPRs.title: Validate known packed storage addresses
topPRs.author: mds1
topPRs.body:
## What
PR #1450 added `storageCodeExceptions` to avoid false positives when storage writes contain packed addresses. That solved the immediate failure by skipping validation for exact `(account, slot)` pairs, but it could also skip checking the address stored in that slot.

## Why
Some Bedrock L1 upgradeable contracts pack an address with smaller fields in the same 32-byte storage slot. The existing state-diff check looks at the full 32-byte value, so packed slots can hide address-shaped values from the normal code/EOA validation. We still want those embedded addresses to be checked.

## How
- Revert the config-driven `storageCodeExceptions` escape hatch.
- Hard-code the known packed slots from the checked-in Bedrock storage layout snapshots.
- For registry-identified known slots, extract the packed 20-byte address and run the existing code/EOA validation on it.
- Leave all other storage writes on the existing full-word validation path.
- Add unit coverage for extraction, ignored stale slots, code-exception behavior, and avoiding over-application to unregistered new contracts.

## Verification
- `mise exec -- forge fmt src/tasks/MultisigTask.sol test/tasks/MultisigTask.t.sol test/tasks/mock/MockMultisigTask.sol`
- `mise exec -- forge test --match-contract MultisigTaskUnitTest --match-test testPackedStorageAddress|testCheckStateDiff -vv`

topPRs.title: fix(SetDisputeGameImpl): zero initBonds(8) on CANNON_KONA disable path
topPRs.author: Wazabie
topPRs.body:
## Summary

The kona disable branch in `SetDisputeGameImpl._setKonaImplementation` (`impl == 0`) cleared `gameImpls[CANNON_KONA]` and `gameArgs[CANNON_KONA]` but left `initBonds[CANNON_KONA]` untouched. Two compounding causes:

1. The disable branch **early-returns** before the bond-setting block (`return;` at the old line 150).
2. The bond-setting block was guarded by `k.bond != 0` — i.e. `bond = 0` in TOML is the "skip" sentinel used across this template (see [091/config.toml:52](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/blob/main/src/tasks/sep/091-alpha-set-dispute-game-impl-permissionless/config.toml#L52) for the same convention on PDG). So even without the early-return, you could not zero a bond from the TOML.

The post-disable validator (`_validateKona`) also only asserted that `gameArgs` was empty, so a residual `initBonds[CANNON_KONA]` passed simulation cleanly.

## Live evidence

Observed today on **karst-u19-beta-0** (Sepolia, DGF `0x313bcDa9f2D76Bab3554436a434A41779dAC74d0`) after [task 095](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/tree/main/src/tasks/sep/095-beta-0-zero-cannon-kona-game-type) ran:

| field | observed | expected |
|---|---|---|
| `gameImpls(8)` | `0x0` | `0x0` ✅ |
| `gameArgs(8)` | `0x` | `0x` ✅ |
| `initBonds(8)` | **`80000000000000000` (0.08 ETH)** | **`0`** ❌ |

The slot is inert (no one can call `create(8, …)` with `gameImpls(8) == 0`), so this is *functionally* harmless. But it's dead state that diverges from the disable path's intent and from what the task config thought it was producing (the task set `bond = 0` in the kona section assuming that meant \"set to zero\" — it meant \"skip\").

## The fix

- `_setKonaImplementation` disable branch: require `k.bond == 0` in the supplied config (consistency with the existing `k.gameArgs.length == 0` requirement), and call `factory.setInitBond(CANNON_KONA, 0)` when the on-chain bond is non-zero (idempotent otherwise).
- `_validateKona` disable case: also require `factory.initBonds(CANNON_KONA) == 0`.

Both changes are scoped to the disable path; the wire/update path is unchanged.

## Out of scope (worth follow-ups)

- The same \"`bond = 0` means skip\" sentinel applies to `_setInitBonds` for FDG and PDG (`SetDisputeGameImpl.sol:188-195`). If anyone ever wants to zero an FDG/PDG bond via this template, the same gap exists there. I left it untouched because there's no live evidence of it biting, and changing the semantics of `fdgBond/pdgBond = 0` would be a behaviour break for existing in-flight tasks (e.g. 091, 095, 096 all use it as a deliberate \"don't touch\" sentinel).
- The sibling [`SetDisputeGameArgs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/blob/main/src/template/SetDisputeGameArgs.sol#L56) template has a proper `bool setBond` flag that disambiguates \"skip\" from \"set to 0\". If/when we migrate kona-disable tasks to `SetDisputeGameArgs`, that's the cleaner long-term home.

## Cleanup for beta-0 itself

This PR doesn't retroactively zero the residual bond on beta-0; that needs a one-shot tx (e.g. via `SetDisputeGameArgs` with `{chainId=420110023, gameType=8, impl=0x0, bond=0}` once that template is taught to call `setInitBond(_, 0)` on disable, or a direct `factory.setInitBond(8, 0)` PAO Safe tx). Filing separately.

## Test plan

- [x] `forge build src/template/SetDisputeGameImpl.sol --skip test` — compiles clean
- [ ] Existing regression tests (`testRegressionCallDataMatches_SetDisputeGameImpl{,_Kona}`) — they exercise only the wire/update path (impl != 0), so behaviour is unchanged. (Couldn't run them locally — pinned forks need archive RPC; CI will.)
- [ ] Consider adding a new example task under `test/tasks/example/sep/` that exercises the kona disable path so the regression suite picks it up going forward.
